events.summary: H1 is the leading hypothesis and its internal telemetry is thoroughly grounded: exchange-gateway connect timeouts to api.exchange-partner.example start 11:01:25Z (F10), ~80s before order-service's first 504 (F9); gateway p99 pins at its 5000ms bound (F17) and upstream_error_rate to the partner stays ~45% (F18); every order-service error is a downstream 'exchange-gateway 504 (placeOrder)' (F9,F16); the v2.15.2 rollback produced zero recovery while the gateway stayed broken (F14,F15); and H2/H3/H4 are each rejected by direct measurement. However, the one fact that decides the FIX is unresolved: H1 (external partner degraded) vs H5 (exchange-gateway's own egress/DNS path broken) produce byte-identical internal telemetry, and the final round could not separate them. Round 3 returned no second direct vantage point to the partner (F42,F48), no successful partner call or probe anywhere (F41,F53), no pod/instance tag to detect a per-node egress fault (F37), and — decisively — all four infra/network metric queries (DNS latency, pod restarts, interface drops, egress bytes) failed with budget_exhausted (F44), so the network layer was never measured. No partner status/notice source exists (F50,F53). The only 'discriminators' are negative (no DNS/TLS error signatures) and a few partner-signed 503s, both of which H1's own assumptions concede are equally consistent with a gateway-side egress proxy or partial-path fault. With tool budget at zero, two hypotheses naming different origins and implying different remediations (partner failover/secondary route vs network/gateway repair) cannot be separated; this is genuinely inconclusive rather than merely under-confident.
